status: Frozen R1 scope correction; supersedes the inferred V1 requirements in the earlier dual-context audit, preserving its backend source facts.

supersedes_as_v1_gate.disposition: Those sections describe an optional independently positioned ground-lighting extension. They are not prerequisites for the requested bounded R1 contact adaptation. The old receipt is retained unchanged.

contract: R1 blends completed mesh and ground total/direct RGB after object material modulation, not albedo or normals before a shared object-light calculation.

Ground art comes from the folded strip. The ground receiver is a copy of NativeOutput i with only worldNormal and pointMaterial=1 changed. Position, shadow position, light-list location, emissive shadow-bypass policy and other receiver flags remain those of the object.
The ground normal is the height-field gradient at the object’s unfolded XY, using height samples at +/-0.5 m. It is not a complete copy of native terrain fragment relief/BSDF.

Point-light direction, squared-distance falloff and world-XY light-grid selection therefore remain at the object. The grid preserves all intersecting frame lights in ascending order by coarsening cells rather than truncating lists.

Point-shadow lookup retains object shadowPosition but recalculates bias/incidence with the copied ground normal. Sun and cloud visibility are reused from the object; they are not resampled at folded ground.

Ground material is neutral and uses terrain-facing response. Ground total=art*(saturate(max(ambient,directional)+local)+glow); direct omits ambient. Both completed RGB branches use lerp(mesh,ground,weight)*dark.

The blend uses existing native combiner RGB with no contact-specific transfer conversion. Ordinary native textures use non-sRGB UNORM formats. Water/bed transmission, alpha test, ambient-share extraction, fog and AO processing remain after this colour blend; object alpha is preserved.
v1_scope_judgment: Required: bounded folded texture integration, object-material-independent ground weight/colour, ground-specific normal/material response, unchanged alpha/upper surfaces, and meaningful near-light/shadow visual controls.

Actual bounded adaptation issue: the copied ground currently inherits the figure-facing directional shadow guard. Give it the terrain shadow transfer using the same object ATTENUATION; retain the original figure guard. No light-position/list/engine change is required.

The explicit four native EI light channels and precise normal/E/k/rain/track reconstruction are remake integration choices. Their strict data/normal tests remain useful and failures remain recorded, but they do not imply pixel-identical complete terrain rendering at a different receiver position.

Optional additional work: independent folded-ground light/shadow position, projected-ground clustered/instance light lists, exact native terrain shadow-bias interpolation across Godot backends, independent full accumulation/fog/BSDF parity. Do not make these V1 adoption gates.

R1’s separate point-shadow normal bias is an exact-fidelity difference from reusing Godot ATTENUATION. Record that approximation and inspect visible behavior; this does not justify the larger displaced-receiver architecture.

The earlier below-wall point-light example must not demand illumination as if the band were a separate ground receiver: R1 also evaluates direction and falloff at the wall. Near-light controls should test material/normal response and bounded stable shadows.
new_work_authorized: Scratch directional-only shadow-transfer variant and fixture preparation. No canonical changes, package edits, or rendered run in this receipt.
